notes: Coverage: 30 easy / 40 medium / 20 hard, 90 total, all distinct titles, eras 1970-2022, 12 TV titles (Friends, Breaking Bad, The Office, GoT, Stranger Things, Squid Game, Queen's Gambit, Sopranos, Mad Men, X-Files, Wednesday, Succession, The Crown, HIMYM, Witcher, Seinfeld, Mandalorian, Ted Lasso, Twin Peaks, The Wire, M*A*S*H, Frasier). Verify at import (less than fully certain): exact tagline wording for Cool Runnings ("One dream. Four Jamaicans. Twenty below zero."), Taxi Driver, and Edward Scissorhands (posters had variant taglines); "Who ya gonna call?" is the theme-song hook used in marketing rather than the printed poster tagline; the Billy Idol T-1000 story and Gibson-passed-on-Gladiator note are widely reported but anecdotal, so consider softening or cutting those two notes; Color Purple's 0-for-11 is correct but confirm phrasing (tied with The Turning Point). All Oscar counts (ROTK 11, Amadeus 8), season counts (M*A*S*H 11, HIMYM 9), and release years were chosen to be stable historical facts.

items.q: Who played Jack Dawson in Titanic (1997)?
items.note: DiCaprio wasn't nominated for an Oscar for Titanic, despite the film winning 11.

items.q: Who played Tony Stark in Iron Man (2008)?
items.note: Downey improvised the final line, 'I am Iron Man.'

items.q: What year did the first Star Wars movie hit theaters?
items.note: It opened in just 32 theaters in the US.

items.q: On Friends, what is the name of the gang's favorite coffee shop?
items.note: Cafe Nervosa is Frasier's spot; MacLaren's is from How I Met Your Mother.

items.q: On Breaking Bad, what subject does Walter White teach?
items.note: Creator Vince Gilligan pitched it as turning Mr. Chips into Scarface.

items.q: Who voiced Buzz Lightyear in Toy Story (1995)?
items.note: Billy Crystal turned down Buzz, then took Mike Wazowski in Monsters, Inc.

items.q: In Jaws, the shark terrorizes which fictional beach town?
items.note: The malfunctioning mechanical shark was nicknamed Bruce.

items.q: What year did Jurassic Park first open in theaters?
items.note: Spielberg released Schindler's List the same year.

items.q: The Office (US) is set in which Pennsylvania city?
items.note: Dunder Mifflin's building in the opening credits is a real Scranton office.

items.q: Who played Hermione Granger in the Harry Potter films?
items.note: Watson was nine years old when she was cast.

items.q: In The Lion King (1994), what is the name of Simba's father?
items.note: James Earl Jones voiced Mufasa in both the 1994 and 2019 versions.

items.q: 'Winter is coming' is the motto of which Game of Thrones house?
items.note: The Lannister sayings are 'Hear Me Roar' and the unofficial one about debts.

items.q: Who played Neo in The Matrix (1999)?
items.note: Will Smith really did turn it down, choosing Wild Wild West instead.

items.q: Stranger Things takes place in which fictional Indiana town?
items.note: Derry is Stephen King's cursed town from It.

items.q: Rocky (1976) is set in which American city?
items.note: Tourists still run the museum steps he trained on.

items.q: Who played the title role in Forrest Gump (1994)?
items.note: Hanks won back-to-back Best Actor Oscars for Philadelphia and Forrest Gump.

items.q: In Finding Nemo, what kind of fish is Nemo?
items.note: Dory the blue tang got her own movie 13 years later.

items.q: Squid Game comes from which country?
items.note: Creator Hwang Dong-hyuk wrote the script more than a decade before Netflix bought it.

items.q: Who played Captain Jack Sparrow in Pirates of the Caribbean?
items.note: Depp based the character partly on Rolling Stone Keith Richards, who later played Jack's father.

items.q: In Frozen, what is the name of Elsa's younger sister?
items.note: 'Let It Go' was written in a single day by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez.

items.q: Who played Katniss Everdeen in The Hunger Games?
items.note: Lawrence was 21 when the first film shot; Katniss is 16 in the book.

items.q: In E.T., what does the alien famously want to do?
items.note: Those Reese's Pieces? M&M's turned the product placement down first.

items.q: Who played the Joker in The Dark Knight (2008)?
items.note: Ledger won a posthumous Oscar, the first acting win for a comic-book movie.

items.q: What year does Marty McFly leave in Back to the Future?
items.note: He travels back to 1955, the year his parents met.

items.q: Who played Danny Zuko in Grease (1978)?
items.note: Richard Gere had played Danny in the London stage production.

items.q: What kind of creature is Shrek?
items.note: Shrek won the first ever Oscar for Best Animated Feature.

items.q: 'Who ya gonna call?' sold which 1984 movie?
items.note: Ray Parker Jr.'s theme song spent three weeks at number one.

items.q: The Queen's Gambit is about a prodigy in which game?
items.note: Chess set sales spiked worldwide after the show dropped in 2020.

items.q: How many people are in Danny Ocean's crew in Ocean's Eleven (2001)?
items.note: The sequels kept counting: Ocean's Twelve, then Ocean's Thirteen.

items.q: Who plays the wisecracking mercenary in Deadpool (2016)?
items.note: Reynolds first played a very different Deadpool in 2009's X-Men Origins: Wolverine.

items.q: Who played mob boss Tony Soprano on The Sopranos?
items.note: Gandolfini was a virtual unknown when HBO cast him in 1999.

items.q: What year was The Godfather released?
items.note: Its sequel arrived just two years later and also won Best Picture.

items.q: How many Infinity Stones does Thanos collect in Avengers: Infinity War?
items.note: Space, Mind, Reality, Power, Time, and Soul.

items.q: Who played the Dude in The Big Lebowski (1998)?
items.note: There's a real religion inspired by the character called Dudeism.

items.q: Who played ad man Don Draper on Mad Men?
items.note: Hamm auditioned while working as a set dresser on other people's shows... okay, as a waiter.

items.q: 'You'll believe a man can fly' was the tagline for which 1978 movie?
items.note: Marlon Brando reportedly earned millions for under 20 minutes of screen time.

items.q: 'The truth is out there' is the slogan of which TV series?
items.note: The poster hangs in Mulder's basement office.

items.q: What year was The Shawshank Redemption released?
items.note: It flopped in theaters, losing the Best Picture race to Forrest Gump.

items.q: What year did Goodfellas come out?
items.note: It lost Best Picture to Dances with Wolves.

items.q: Who played FBI trainee Clarice Starling in The Silence of the Lambs?
items.note: Anthony Hopkins won Best Actor with roughly 16 minutes of screen time.

items.q: Who starred as a man unknowingly living on a TV set in The Truman Show?
items.note: 'Truman Show delusion' became a term real psychiatrists use.

items.q: How many Oscars did The Return of the King win?
items.note: Eleven for eleven: it won every category it was nominated in.

items.q: Who plays Wednesday Addams in Netflix's Wednesday?
items.note: Ortega choreographed the viral dance scene herself.

items.q: What is the last name of the family battling over the company in Succession?
items.note: Waystar Royco is the company; Logan is the dad's first name.

items.q: Who won an Oscar for the title role in Erin Brockovich (2000)?
items.note: The real Erin Brockovich has a cameo as a waitress named Julia.

items.q: 'Be afraid. Be very afraid.' was the tagline for which 1986 remake?
items.note: Geena Davis says the line in the movie, and it became a catchphrase.

items.q: What year was Fight Club released?
items.note: 1999 also gave us The Matrix, The Sixth Sense, and American Beauty.

items.q: Who wrote and directed Get Out (2017)?
items.note: Peele won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay with his debut feature.

items.q: Who directed Parasite (2019)?
items.note: Parasite was the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture.

items.q: How many emotions run Riley's head in Pixar's Inside Out (2015)?
items.note: Joy, Sadness, Fear, Anger, and Disgust; the sequel added more.

items.q: Who played Queen Elizabeth II in the first two seasons of The Crown?
items.note: All three listed queens eventually played her as the show recast with age.

items.q: How many seasons did How I Met Your Mother run?
items.note: The mother doesn't fully appear until the season 8 finale.

items.q: How many students serve Saturday detention in The Breakfast Club?
items.note: A brain, an athlete, a basket case, a princess, and a criminal.

items.q: 'Escape or die frying' was the tagline for which animated film?
items.note: It's basically The Great Escape with claymation chickens.

items.q: 'The first casualty of war is innocence' sold which 1986 film?
choices: Born on the Fourth of July
items.note: Oliver Stone based it on his own tour in Vietnam.

items.q: What year did the first Avengers movie assemble in theaters?
items.note: It was the first film to be built from five separate franchise lead-ins.

items.q: Who played icy editor Miranda Priestly in The Devil Wears Prada?
items.note: The character is widely read as a riff on Vogue's Anna Wintour.

items.q: Who played Geralt of Rivia in the first three seasons of The Witcher?
items.note: Cavill, a fan of the games, lobbied hard for the part, then handed it to a Hemsworth.

items.q: What year did Seinfeld premiere?
items.note: The pilot was called The Seinfeld Chronicles and nearly wasn't picked up.

items.q: In Whiplash (2014), what instrument does Andrew obsessively practice?
items.note: J.K. Simmons won an Oscar for hurling insults (and a chair) at him.

items.q: What is the real name of 'Baby Yoda' in The Mandalorian?
items.note: Din is actually the Mandalorian himself: Din Djarin.

items.q: In Slumdog Millionaire, Jamal competes on which quiz show?
choices: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire
items.note: The film won eight Oscars including Best Picture.

items.q: Who played General Maximus in Gladiator (2000)?
items.note: Mel Gibson reportedly passed on the role before Crowe took it.

items.q: In Home Alone, what do burglars Harry and Marv call themselves?
items.note: They rebrand as the Sticky Bandits in the sequel.

items.q: Who played Bible-quoting hitman Jules in Pulp Fiction?
items.note: The Ezekiel 25:17 speech is mostly invented; only a few words match the real verse.

items.q: Who played the Bride in Kill Bill?
items.note: Zoe Bell was actually Thurman's stunt double on the film.

items.q: What year was Saving Private Ryan released?
items.note: Its Omaha Beach opening reportedly sent some veterans out of theaters.

items.q: Complete the Sixth Sense line: 'I see ___ ___.'
items.note: Haley Joel Osment was nominated for an Oscar at age 11.

items.q: 'One dream. Four Jamaicans. Twenty below zero.' sold which comedy?
items.note: Loosely based on Jamaica's real 1988 Olympic bobsled team.

items.q: On Ted Lasso, what sport does Ted coach at AFC Richmond?
items.note: The character began as a promo for NBC's Premier League coverage.

items.q: 'On every street in every city, there's a nobody who dreams of being a somebody' sold which film?
items.note: De Niro's 'You talkin' to me?' was improvised.

items.q: 'We are not alone' was the tagline for which 1977 film?
choices: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
items.note: Its five-note alien greeting became one of cinema's most famous melodies.

items.q: 'Man is the warmest place to hide' sold which 1982 horror film?
items.note: John Carpenter's remake flopped in 1982, then became a classic on video.

items.q: 'Love means never having to say you're sorry' comes from which 1970 film?
items.note: Ryan O'Neal himself mocked the line in the 1972 comedy What's Up, Doc?

items.q: What year was Blade Runner released?
items.note: 1982 was stacked: E.T., The Thing, and Tron opened within weeks of each other.

items.q: What year did Chinatown come out?
items.note: Of its 11 Oscar nominations, it won just one, for the screenplay.

items.q: What year did Twin Peaks premiere on ABC?
items.note: 'Who killed Laura Palmer?' became a national obsession that spring.

items.q: What year did Heat pair Pacino and De Niro in theaters?
items.note: Their diner scene was the first time the two shared a frame on screen.

items.q: What year was the Korean thriller Oldboy released?
items.note: The hallway hammer fight was shot as one continuous take.

items.q: Who played Elvira in Scarface (1983)?
items.note: Pfeiffer was a near-unknown; Pacino reportedly favored another actress.

items.q: Who played stick-up man Omar Little on The Wire?
items.note: Barack Obama repeatedly named Omar his favorite TV character.

items.q: Who played the liquid-metal T-1000 in Terminator 2?
items.note: Billy Idol was reportedly considered before a motorcycle crash ruled him out.

items.q: Who played young Vito Corleone in The Godfather Part II?
items.note: De Niro won the Oscar speaking almost entirely Sicilian dialect.

items.q: Who played Nurse Ratched in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest?
items.note: The film swept all five major Oscars, a feat managed only three times ever.

items.q: The Color Purple (1985) got 11 Oscar nominations. How many did it win?
items.note: It tied the record for most nominations without a single win.

items.q: How many seasons did M*A*S*H run?
items.note: The show ran 11 years covering a war that lasted three.

items.q: How many Oscars did Amadeus (1984) win?
items.note: Two of its stars competed against each other for Best Actor; F. Murray Abraham won.

items.q: In The Princess Bride, who is the six-fingered man?
items.note: 'Hello. My name is Inigo Montoya. You killed my father. Prepare to die.'

items.q: Frasier is a spin-off of which sitcom?
items.note: Frasier Crane appeared in over 400 combined episodes across the two shows.

items.q: 'His story will touch you, even though he can't' sold which Tim Burton film?
items.note: It was the first of eight collaborations between Burton and Johnny Depp.
